headline: Private credit default rates have only risen from 1% to 1.5%, well below GFC levels of 4-5%, but covenant erosion at the large-cap end is a key risk
reasoning: Valmerana notes that despite media noise, actual default rates in private credit remain modest. He argues the real metric to watch is loss rates, not defaults, and that mid-market direct lenders retaining whole loans negotiate better covenants and achieve higher recovery rates.

headline: Pantheon favours mid-market direct lenders who retain whole loans, citing better spreads, covenants and recovery rates versus large-cap syndicated deals
reasoning: Valmerana highlights that mid-market lenders who hold loans entirely on their own balance sheet can negotiate tighter covenants and better spreads, giving them more control to work proactively with borrowers in stress situations. quote: What we like about the mid-market is that usually the firm that is lending holds that entirely themselves, is able to negotiate not just better spreads, but better covenants and more protections.
